A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MMSI-Bench. Their text, tables, figures, and appendices A–H are available for reliable comparison, including content relocated between the main text and appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports original model and human evaluations, prompting experiments, and automated error-analysis results in Sections 4–5 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds a cross-model correlation analysis relating MMSI-Bench scores to downstream embodied-task performance.

M1.justification: The benchmark construction, prompting procedures, and reference-assisted automated error-analysis pipeline remain unchanged. Additional annotation explanations do not establish a revised method.

E1.justification: Appendix E.5 adds score-based analysis covering EB-Navigation, EB-Manipulation, and EB-Habitat. These substantially extend evaluation coverage to embodied control and active perception. The original MMSI-Bench tasks and eight image sources remain; the PDFs do not establish that downstream experiments were newly run.

E2.justification: New Table 11 includes Claude-3.5-Sonnet, absent from v2's reported comparisons, alongside eight previously evaluated models. The main comparison set and spatially fine-tuned comparators are retained; v2 Table 9 becomes v3 Table 4.

E3.justification: Appendix E.5 introduces a nine-model comparison pairing MMSI-Bench accuracy with three downstream task scores. The original temperature-zero, 2,048-token, exact-match evaluation remains unchanged. Newly disclosed source and split details in F.7 do not establish changed experiments.

E4.justification: v3 adds a downstream-validity analysis testing whether MMSI-Bench scores track embodied-task performance, plus reasoning-depth statistics in F.3. Existing prompting, fine-tuning, error analyses, and case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Appendix E.5 adds Pearson and Spearman correlation estimation across models. It introduces no confidence intervals, significance tests, or repeated-run/seed information; existing human-evaluator counts remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Table 11 adds downstream scores and Claude-3.5-Sonnet's 31.3% MMSI-Bench result; E.5 adds six correlation coefficients, including navigation Pearson 0.8147 and Spearman 0.7333. F.3 newly reports 3–11 reasoning steps, averaging 5.7. Existing performance tables are unchanged, and the reasoning accuracies newly stated in Section 5.2 already appeared in v2 Figure 7.

T1.justification: The spatial-task and error definitions are retained, with no added or revised formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations. The new correlation analysis is empirical.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: a 1,000-question benchmark, a large human–model performance gap, and reference-assisted diagnosis of four error types. The new appendix evidence does not redefine these core claims.

C2.justification: Appendix E.5 newly interprets the correlations as evidence that MMSI-Bench measures capabilities relevant to navigation, manipulation, and active perception. Existing limitations and error explanations remain; the template-based fine-tuning explanation is relocated from the appendix.

D1.justification: F.7 adds task-by-source counts and split/setup details, while F.3 clarifies multi-step annotation. Some new counts conflict internally, such as 84 measurement samples versus source counts totaling 64. The title-page project link is removed and replaced by contact emails; Appendix B.6's access statement remains.

R1.justification: v3 adds EmbodiedBench, Yang et al. (2025), as the reference for downstream comparisons and associated positioning. The existing related-work discussion and spatial-benchmark comparisons are otherwise retained.

P1.justification: Limited restructuring moves the fine-tuning discussion into Section 4.2 and renumbers the prompting-results subsection. v3 also adds explanatory passages, acknowledgments, and conference headers. Most existing prose and the overall narrative structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The fine-tuning table moves from appendix Table 9 to main-text Table 4, and downstream Table 11 is added. Several figures and interface screenshots are repositioned as text reflows. Existing figure content and table structures are retained.

improvement.justification: The new correlations in E.5 agree with Table 11 and provide empirical support for downstream relevance that v2 lacked; reasoning-depth statistics also clarify task difficulty. These are limited gains, tempered by correlation-only evidence, inconsistent new F.7 counts, and removal of the project link. The core benchmark and findings remain stable.
